manual_controls.decision: Three earlier drains and a later culvert are separate successive features. The clogged last drain and replacement route are reported; downtime, causal sediment entry and the organizing institution remain unresolved.

Stage VI follows a reported brief desertion. Retention of wall segments serving some reservoirs, salvage of older stone and changed streets/housing are explicit. The reservoir-support segments are not identified as those of the named East reservoir.

manual_controls.decision: Repair, later filling, activity and cessation of water use are confirmed in the original preliminary PDF. Printed p.164 excludes regular continuous occupation in that activity area. Poverty, religious sanctity and the same fate for all eastern reservoirs remain excavator interpretations.

manual_controls.status: identity and chronology checked; p.104 visually checked
manual_controls.decision: The report is a 2015 preliminary draft. Broad stage dates are primarily stratigraphic/typological with limited and partly inconsistent TL checks. They preserve interruptions and do not supply seasonal repair windows. Archive uploader creator/language and CC0 fields do not control authorship, text language or parent redistribution rights.

The 700 wells are an extrapolation, covers establish possible access, local drain rebuilding is a reported sequence, and no intact full network allowed the cited flow calculation. Connected drains provide a proposed broad co-use test. No annual water or labor account is derived.

The 2011 filename and host item refer to the preceding magazine section. The Jansen chapter belongs to the 2014 edited volume; a 2013 typesetting timestamp is separately retained. Note 1 describes substantial reuse of Jansen 1993.

Roughouts, debris, wear and experimental reconstruction support a tool-production/use chain. The rate table concerns modern experiments, and the apprenticeship statement is an author hypothesis. Ancient training duration, provider count and mineral source are unmeasured.

manual_controls.locus: S09 issue header and pp.4–6; S10 PDF p.5
manual_controls.status: scoped reuse with prior visual inspection documented
manual_controls.decision: S09 is nominal 1996 despite a 1998 filename. Specialized drill loss and alternative source explanations belong to S10, the 2007 synthesis. Its older river/migration narrative was not reused. Modern analogy and reported substitute techniques do not establish an uninterrupted practitioner lineage.

manual_controls.locus: S06 publisher XML Sec2–Sec3, Sec16–Sec18; S07 proof pp.13–19
manual_controls.decision: Community crop diversity, sequential use of the same field, intercropping and independent supply routes are different propositions. Seasonal remains and weeds support constrained reconstruction; material/practice variation predates contraction. Data overlap across these works.

Manufacturing traces differ from the inferred collector/distribution organization. Later occupation and ending craft/network indicators are reported together at broad phase resolution. Original issue is 2005; the publisher's 2026 migration date is separately retained. No population or annual production is derived from area or stockpiles.

manual_controls.locus: Publisher XML §§2.1, 4.1, 4.3–4.4, 5 and Table 4; PDF title
manual_controls.decision: Final volume is 125. Text sample count is 172; Table 4 site counts sum to 171. The discrepancy remains unresolved. Non-detection of period differences is not a prospective equivalence test; isotope mixtures and reference baselines limit ingredient specificity. No new significance calculation was performed.

160 examined minus 45 excluded gives 115 analytic individuals. Burial and preservation selection prevent a living-population prevalence estimate. Area G is relatively placed from ceramics without independent absolute dating. Social vulnerability explanations remain author interpretations.

Northeastern reoccupation and absence of later sites require revisitation and gap closure; the authors explicitly consider survey artifacts. Broad phase-assigned locations are not simultaneous populations or identified migration groups.

manual_controls.status: automated joins and hashes passed; manual dependence review recorded
manual_controls.decision: Editions and source formats do not become new archaeological evidence. Provenance groups have partial cross-group overlap and are not an effective sample size. All six service/schedule measurement fields remain null in all 34 observation records; zero quantitative eligibility follows from that gate, not from an estimated historical deficit.
